experiment_contract.parent_child: retrieve/rerank 256/32 children nested under 1024/128 parents; deliver deduplicated parents
experiment_contract.selection: hard gates first; no weighted aggregate score

baseline-512.answer:
The notifications about the Sweet v. DeVos lawsuit are sent to borrower defense applicants who are potential members of the group of borrowers to whom the lawsuit applies, to inform them that there is a proposed settlement of the lawsuit.
The settlement will not become final until it is approved by the court as fair, adequate, and reasonable, and the notification describes how borrowers' legal rights may be affected by the settlement.
The lawsuit challenges the fact that ED did not issue a final decision on any borrower defense applications from any school between June 2018 and December 2019, and is only about that failure to issue final decisions, not whether those applications should result in loan cancellation.
Both parties are proposing to settle the lawsuit, and this proposed settlement is a compromise of disputed claims, with ED continuing to deny that it has acted unlawfully.

To get your Social Security Benefit Verification Letter online, log in to your my Social Security account for instant access.
The benefit verification letter (also called a benefits letter or Social Security award letter) serves as proof of your retirement, disability, Supplemental Security Income (SSI), or Medicare benefits, and can also serve as proof that you have applied for benefits or have never received Social Security benefits or SSI.
You may use the letter as proof for loans, housing assistance, mortgage, and other income verification purposes. It includes your name, date of birth, and the benefit you receive.
If you already have a my Social Security account, sign in and go to Replacement Documents on the right side of the screen, then choose 'Get a Benefit Verification Letter' to view, save, and print your personalized letter.
If you don't have an account, creating a free my Social Security account takes less than 10 minutes and lets you download or print your benefit verification letter.
For help, call the toll-free number 1-800-772-1213 or visit your Social Security office. If you are deaf or hard of hearing, call the TTY number 1-800-325-0778 between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m., Monday through Friday.

baseline-512.answer:
If you disagree with ED's decision on your borrower defense claim, you can ask ED to reconsider your application.
You can request reconsideration by sending a new email with the subject line "Request for Reconsideration" to BorrowerDefense@ed.gov, including the number that appears with the words "Request for Reconsideration" in the "What if I don't agree with this decision?" section of your notification email.
Alternatively, you can mail your request to U.S. Department of Education, P.O. Box 1854, Monticello, KY 42633.
In your request for reconsideration, you should provide what you think was decided incorrectly, why you believe the decision was incorrect, and any evidence that establishes you are eligible for a different decision.
ED will not accept any request for reconsideration that includes new allegations of misconduct by your school; such a request will be rejected, and you must file a new application for any new allegations.
ED will not place your federal student loans into forbearance or stopped collection activity when you file a request for reconsideration.
If your borrower defense claim was approved, ED will not begin its review of your request for reconsideration until your federal loan servicer notifies you that the discharge has been applied.
If you have questions about your notification email, you can call the borrower defense hotline at 1-855-279-6207, available Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Eastern time.

baseline-512.answer:
If you are issued a ticket for a non-criminal moving traffic violation in the five boroughs of New York City, it will be handled by a New York State DMV Traffic Violations Bureau (TVB). TVBs do not handle parking violations.
Follow the instructions on the ticket for the plea you wish to make, and act promptly. If you don't answer the ticket in the time allowed, your driver license will be suspended, and you could later be found guilty because of your failure to respond (a default conviction).
To plead not guilty, check the "not guilty" box on the back of the ticket, fill in the requested information, sign it, and mail the ticket to the Albany address listed. DMV will send you a letter telling you when and where to go for your hearing.
To plead guilty, check the "guilty" box on the back of the ticket, fill in the requested information, sign it, and either mail it with your payment to the Albany address listed on the ticket or bring your payment to any TVB office.
You may not plead guilty by mail if the charge will result in license or registration suspension or revocation upon conviction (such as driving without insurance or a third speeding violation within 18 months). If you plead guilty to such a charge by mail, you will be notified that you must go to the TVB to answer the charge in person.

baseline-512.answer:
The law requires an adjustment to your monthly Medicare Part B medical insurance and Medicare prescription drug coverage premiums, but this affects less than five percent of people with Medicare, and most people don't pay higher premiums.
For most beneficiaries, the government pays a substantial portion (about 75 percent) of the Part B premium, and the beneficiary pays the remaining 25 percent.
If you are a higher-income beneficiary, you'll pay a larger percentage of the total cost of Part B — 35, 50, 65, 80, or 85 percent — depending on what you report to the IRS.
The standard Part B premium for 2020 is $144.60.
If you file your taxes as married filing jointly and your MAGI is greater than $170,000, you'll pay higher premiums; if you file using a different status and your MAGI is greater than $85,000, you'll pay higher premiums.
For higher-income beneficiaries with Medicare prescription drug coverage, the additional amount is based on a base premium (not your own plan premium) and is deducted from your monthly Social Security payments; if it exceeds your payment or you don't get monthly payments, you'll receive a separate bill from another federal agency.

baseline-512.answer:
Yes. If you have an adverse credit history, one option to become eligible for a Direct PLUS Loan is to document extenuating circumstances relating to that adverse credit history.
To do this, you must provide a statement explaining your extenuating circumstances along with applicable documentation to support your claim.
The Secretary may use discretion to consider whether your extenuating circumstances allow you to qualify for a loan, but review does not guarantee approval, and previous approval does not guarantee further approvals.
Loss of a job or a poor economy alone are generally not considered extenuating circumstances.
Examples of extenuating circumstances and their required documentation include: a charged-off or collection account, a discharged Chapter 7/11/12 bankruptcy (timing issue or chapter conversion), and a state/county/federal tax lien (satisfactory repayment arrangement, inclusion in Chapter 13 bankruptcy, incorrectly filed lien, released lien, or proof of payment).
If you document extenuating circumstances to the Department's satisfaction, you must also complete PLUS Credit Counseling.
If you no longer wish to document extenuating circumstances, your options include obtaining an endorser and completing PLUS Credit Counseling, notifying your school's financial aid office, or not pursuing a Direct PLUS Loan at this time.

baseline-512.answer:
Yes, in certain situations you can qualify for 5 years of free VA health care. If you served in combat after the Gulf War or in combat against a hostile force after November 11, 1998, you don't have to provide your income to qualify for 5 years of free VA health care for any illness that may be related to your military service.
Returning OEF/OIF/OND combat Veterans can receive free VA health care for up to 5 years after discharge or release for any condition related to their service in Operation Enduring Freedom (OEF) in Afghanistan, Operation Iraqi Freedom (OIF), or Operation New Dawn (OND) in Iraq. This is called an enhanced eligibility period.

Yes, there is a limit to the amount a family can receive each month. The limit varies, but it is generally equal to between 150 and 180 percent of the basic benefit rate.

Any benefits paid to a surviving divorced spouse based on disability or age won't count toward this maximum amount.

baseline-512.answer:
The standard Part B premium for 2020 is $144.60.
If you have a higher income, you'll pay an additional income-related monthly adjustment amount for Medicare Part B and Medicare prescription drug coverage. Higher-income beneficiaries pay monthly Part B premiums equal to 35%, 50%, 65%, 80%, or 85% of the total cost, depending on what you report to the IRS.
For Medicare prescription drug coverage, higher-income beneficiaries pay monthly premiums plus an additional amount based on what they report to the IRS, determined using a base premium.
If you file taxes as married filing jointly and your MAGI is greater than $170,000, or if you file using a different status and your MAGI is greater than $85,000, you'll pay higher premiums.

baseline-512.answer:
Your AGI will be used if you filed a federal income tax return in the past two years AND your current income isn't significantly different from the income reported on your most recent federal income tax return.
You can provide your AGI by applying online using the Income-Driven Repayment Plan Request and using the IRS Data Retrieval Tool to transfer income information from your federal tax return.
Alternatively, you can use the paper Income-Driven Repayment Plan Request and provide a paper copy of your most recently filed federal income tax return or an IRS tax return transcript.

baseline-512.answer:
If you filed a federal income tax return for the year in question, you need to show us your signed copy of the return.
To determine your income-related monthly adjustment amounts, we use your most recent federal tax return the IRS provides to us. Generally, this information is from a tax return filed in 2019 for tax year 2018, but sometimes the IRS only provides information from a return filed in 2018 for tax year 2017.
If we use the 2017 tax year data, and you filed a return for tax year 2018 or did not need to file a tax return for tax year 2018, call us or visit any local Social Security office so we can update our records.
If you amended your tax return and it changes the income used to determine your income-related monthly adjustment amounts (your MAGI), let us know. Social Security needs to see a copy of the amended tax return you filed and your acknowledgment receipt from the IRS.

baseline-512.answer:
Yes, you can file a claim for additional disability compensation by mail or fax. VA encourages filing online, but if you can't or don't want to file online, you can file by mail or fax.
For a child under 18 years of age, you'll need to fill out a Declaration of Status of Dependents (VA Form 21-686c).
Mail your completed form to: Department of Veterans Affairs, Evidence Intake Center, PO Box 4444, Janesville, WI 53547-4444. Or fax it to 844-531-7817 if you live in the U.S.

baseline-512.answer:
If a child is age 18 or older, Social Security will evaluate the disability the same way as for any adult, and the application is sent to the Disability Determination Services in your state.
If the adult child receives benefits as an adult disabled since childhood, the benefits generally end if he or she gets married, though some marriages (for example, to another adult disabled child) are considered protected; the rules vary by situation.
If the child is still a full-time student at a secondary or elementary school at age 18, benefits will continue until the child graduates or until two months after the child becomes age 19, whichever is first.
If the child is disabled, completing an Adult Disability Report and having it available at the time of the appointment can speed up the application process.

baseline-512.answer:
FFEL Program loans are not eligible for discharge under the Borrower Defense to Repayment law or regulations.
If you want your borrower defense discharge to apply to your FFEL loans, you can consolidate them into a Direct Consolidation Loan and obtain the discharge.
To apply for a Direct Consolidation Loan, go to StudentAid.gov/app/launchConsolidation.action, then contact the borrower defense hotline at 1-855-279-6207 (8 a.m. to 8 p.m. ET, Monday through Friday) to proceed with discharge.

baseline-512.answer:
FFEL Program loans and Federal Perkins Loan Program loans are not eligible for discharge under the Borrower Defense to Repayment law or regulations.
If you want your borrower defense discharge to apply to your FFEL and/or Federal Perkins loans, you can consolidate them into a Direct Consolidation Loan and obtain the discharge.
To apply for a Direct Consolidation Loan, go to StudentAid.gov/app/launchConsolidation.action.
Once you have your Direct Consolidation Loan, contact the borrower defense hotline at 1-855-279-6207 (Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. ET) to proceed with discharge.

baseline-512.answer:
Yes, you can keep your CDL with restrictions. Your CDL will have the restrictions for the driving type you certify to.
For example, if you are eligible for Excepted Intrastate operation (EA), you must ensure your CDL has the required restrictions: K (CDL Intrastate Only) and A3 (Med Cert Exempt).
If you expect to operate in an excepted driving type (EA or EI), a Medical Examiner's Certificate is not required, but you will need to have the appropriate restrictions (A3 and/or K) added to your driver's license.
If your driving type changes, you must go to a local DMV office to change your self-certification driving type and have your license amended to add or delete the appropriate restrictions.

baseline-512.answer:
Yes. You can get support from resources offered by other government departments and community organizations outside of VA, such as Military OneSource (visit the Military OneSource website or call 800-342-9647 anytime), the Psychological Health Resource Center, the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline (800-273-8255), the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention, and SAMHSA.
For Veterans and transitioning service members, you can also visit the Department of Defense (DoD) Military OneSource website or VA's mental health site for transitioning service members.
For job-search help, there are links to more resources outside of VA for Veterans, as well as career resources for spouses and other family members of Veterans and service members.
Other VA benefits and services include GI Bill benefits, other educational assistance programs, home loans, and life insurance.

The notifications about the Sweet v. DeVos lawsuit are sent to borrower defense applicants who are potential members of the group of borrowers to whom the lawsuit applies, to inform them that there is a proposed settlement of the lawsuit.
The settlement will not become final until it is approved by the court as fair, adequate, and reasonable, and the notification describes how borrowers' legal rights may be affected by the settlement.
The lawsuit challenges the fact that ED did not issue a final decision on any borrower defense applications from any school between June 2018 and December 2019, and is only about that failure to issue final decisions, not whether those applications should result in loan cancellation.
Both parties are proposing to settle the lawsuit, and this proposed settlement is a compromise of disputed claims, with ED continuing to deny that it has acted unlawfully.

To get your Social Security Benefit Verification Letter online, log in to your my Social Security account for instant access.
The benefit verification letter (also called a benefits letter or Social Security award letter) serves as proof of your retirement, disability, Supplemental Security Income (SSI), or Medicare benefits, and can also serve as proof that you have applied for benefits or have never received Social Security benefits or SSI.
You may use the letter as proof for loans, housing assistance, mortgage, and other income verification purposes. It includes your name, date of birth, and the benefit you receive.
If you already have a my Social Security account, sign in and go to Replacement Documents on the right side of the screen, then choose 'Get a Benefit Verification Letter' to view, save, and print your personalized letter.
If you don't have an account, creating a free my Social Security account takes less than 10 minutes and lets you download or print your benefit verification letter.
For help, call the toll-free number 1-800-772-1213 or visit your Social Security office. If you are deaf or hard of hearing, call the TTY number 1-800-325-0778 between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m., Monday through Friday.

If you disagree with ED's decision on your borrower defense claim, you can ask ED to reconsider your application.
You can request reconsideration by sending a new email with the subject line "Request for Reconsideration" to BorrowerDefense@ed.gov, including the number that appears with the words "Request for Reconsideration" in the "What if I don't agree with this decision?" section of your notification email.
Alternatively, you can mail your request to U.S. Department of Education, P.O. Box 1854, Monticello, KY 42633.
In your request for reconsideration, you should provide what you think was decided incorrectly, why you believe the decision was incorrect, and any evidence that establishes you are eligible for a different decision.
ED will not accept any request for reconsideration that includes new allegations of misconduct by your school; such a request will be rejected, and you must file a new application for any new allegations.
ED will not place your federal student loans into forbearance or stopped collection activity when you file a request for reconsideration.
If your borrower defense claim was approved, ED will not begin its review of your request for reconsideration until your federal loan servicer notifies you that the discharge has been applied.
If you have questions about your notification email, you can call the borrower defense hotline at 1-855-279-6207, available Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Eastern time.

Follow the instructions on the ticket for the plea you wish to make, and act promptly. If you don't answer the ticket in the time allowed, your driver license will be suspended.
If you are issued a ticket for a non-criminal moving traffic violation in the five boroughs of New York City, it will be handled by a New York State DMV Traffic Violations Bureau (TVB). TVBs do not handle parking violations.
To plead not guilty, check the "not guilty" box on the back of the ticket, fill in the requested information, sign it, and mail the ticket to the Albany address listed. DMV will send you a letter telling you when and where to go for your hearing.
To plead guilty, check the "guilty" box on the back of the ticket, fill in the requested information, sign it, and either mail it with your payment to the Albany address listed on the ticket or bring your payment to any TVB office.

conditional-parent-child.answer:
The law requires an adjustment to your monthly Medicare Part B medical insurance and Medicare prescription drug coverage premiums, but this affects less than five percent of people with Medicare, and most people don't pay higher premiums.
For most beneficiaries, the government pays a substantial portion (about 75 percent) of the Part B premium, and the beneficiary pays the remaining 25 percent.
If you have higher income, you'll pay an additional amount called the income-related monthly adjustment amount. For Part B, you'll pay monthly premiums equal to 35, 50, 65, 80, or 85 percent of the total cost, depending on what you report to the IRS.
For Medicare prescription drug coverage, higher-income beneficiaries pay monthly premiums plus an additional amount based on what they report to the IRS, determined using a base premium rather than their own plan premium.
The standard Part B premium for 2020 is $144.60.
Social Security uses your most recent federal tax return and a sliding scale based on your modified adjusted gross income (MAGI). If you file married filing jointly and your MAGI is greater than $170,000, or if you file using a different status and your MAGI is greater than $85,000, you'll pay higher premiums.
If you must pay higher premiums, Social Security will send you a letter with your premium amount and the reason for the determination.

Yes. If you have extenuating circumstances relating to the adverse credit history, you may provide a statement explaining those circumstances along with applicable documentation to support your claim.
The Secretary can use discretion and, based on your circumstances, consider whether extenuating circumstances allow you to qualify for a loan. Review does not guarantee approval, and previous approval does not guarantee further approvals.
Loss of a job, poor economy, etc. alone are generally not considered extenuating circumstances.
Examples of extenuating circumstances and required proof include: being an authorized user on the account, the account being paid in full, a satisfactory repayment arrangement with six months of on-time payments, inclusion in a Chapter 13 bankruptcy, debt consolidation, and divorce (for 90+ days delinquent debts).
Additional documentation may be required beyond the basic requirements listed.

If you filed a federal income tax return in the past two years and your current income isn't significantly different from the income reported on your most recent federal income tax return, your AGI will be used. You can provide your AGI by applying online using the IRS Data Retrieval Tool, or by submitting a paper Income-Driven Repayment Plan Request with a paper copy of your most recently filed federal income tax return or an IRS tax return transcript.
If you haven't filed a federal income tax return in the past two years, or if your current income is significantly different from the income reported on your most recent federal income tax return (for example, if you lost your job or experienced a drop in income), alternative documentation of your income will be used instead.
To provide alternative documentation: if you currently receive taxable income, you must submit a paper Income-Driven Repayment Plan Request with alternative documentation such as a pay stub; if you currently have no income or only untaxed income, you can indicate that on the online or paper application and are not required to supply further documentation.

conditional-parent-child.answer:
For a child under age 18, we don't need to consider the child's disability when deciding if he or she qualifies for benefits as your dependent. The child's benefits normally stop at age 18 unless he or she is a full-time student in an elementary or high school (benefits can continue until age 19) or is disabled.
To apply for a child under age 18, you will need to complete an Application for Supplemental Security Income (SSI) and a Child Disability Report. At this time, only the Child Disability Report can be completed online; contact Social Security by phone or in person to schedule an appointment to complete the SSI application.
You can review the Child Disability Starter Kit, which answers common questions about applying for SSI benefits for children and includes a worksheet to help gather the information you need. You should also contact Social Security right away to find out whether the income and resources of the parents and the child are within the allowed limits.
You can call toll-free at 1-800-772-1213, or the TTY number 1-800-325-0778 if you are deaf or hard of hearing. Representatives are available Monday through Friday between 8 a.m. and 5:30 p.m.

Yes, you can keep your CDL with restrictions. Your CDL will have the restrictions for the driving type you certify to.
For example, if you are eligible for Excepted Intrastate operation (EA), you can keep your CDL but must ensure it has the required restrictions: K (CDL Intrastate Only) and A3 (Med Cert Exempt).
If you expect to operate in an excepted driving type (EA or EI), a Medical Examiner's Certificate is not required, but you will need to have the appropriate restrictions (A3 and/or K) added to your driver's license.
If your driving type changes, you must go to a local DMV office to change your self-certification driving type and have your license amended to add or delete the appropriate restrictions.

The notifications are sent because the Sweet v. DeVos lawsuit challenges the fact that the U.S. Department of Education (ED) did not issue a final decision on any borrower defense applications from any school between June 2018 and December 2019.
The lawsuit is only about the fact that final decisions were not issued during that period, not about whether those applications should result in loan cancellation.
Both parties are proposing to settle the lawsuit, and the notifications inform potential class members that there is a proposed settlement, which will not become final until it is approved by the court as fair, adequate, and reasonable.
The notification describes how borrowers' legal rights may be affected by the settlement.

To get your Social Security Benefit Verification Letter online, log in to your my Social Security account for instant access.
The benefit verification letter (also called a benefits letter or Social Security award letter) serves as proof of your retirement, disability, Supplemental Security Income (SSI), or Medicare benefits, and can also serve as proof that you have applied for benefits or have never received Social Security benefits or SSI.
You may use the letter as proof for loans, housing assistance, mortgage, and other income verification purposes. It includes your name, date of birth, and the benefit you receive.
If you already have a my Social Security account, sign in and go to Replacement Documents on the right side of the screen, then choose 'Get a Benefit Verification Letter' to view, save, and print your personalized letter.
If you don't have an account, creating a free my Social Security account takes less than 10 minutes and lets you download or print your benefit verification letter.
For help, call the toll-free number 1-800-772-1213 or visit your Social Security office. If you are deaf or hard of hearing, call the TTY number 1-800-325-0778 between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m., Monday through Friday.

If you disagree with ED's decision on your borrower defense application, you can ask ED to reconsider it.
You can request reconsideration by sending a new email with the subject line "Request for Reconsideration" to BorrowerDefense@ed.gov, including the number that appears with the words "Request for Reconsideration" in the "What if I don't agree with this decision?" section of your notification email.
Alternatively, you can mail your request to U.S. Department of Education, P.O. Box 1854, Monticello, KY 42633.
In your request for reconsideration, provide what you think was decided incorrectly, why you believe the decision was incorrect, and any evidence that establishes you are eligible for a different decision.
ED will not accept any request for reconsideration that includes new allegations of misconduct by your school; such a request will be rejected, and you must file a new application for those new allegations.
ED will not place your federal student loans into forbearance or stopped collection activity when you file a request for reconsideration.
If your borrower defense claim was approved, ED will not begin its review of your request for reconsideration until your federal loan servicer notifies you that the discharge has been completed.
For more information about reconsideration, contact the borrower defense hotline at 1-855-279-6207 from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. ET, Monday through Friday.

If you are issued a ticket for a non-criminal moving traffic violation in the five boroughs of New York City, it will be handled by a New York State DMV Traffic Violations Bureau (TVB).
Follow the instructions on the ticket for the plea you wish to make, and act promptly. If you don't answer the ticket in the time allowed, your driver license will be suspended.
To plead not guilty, check the "not guilty" box on the back of the ticket, fill in the requested information, sign it, and mail the ticket to the Albany address listed. DMV will send you a letter telling you when and where to go for your hearing.
To plead guilty, check the "guilty" box on the back of the ticket, fill in the requested information, sign it, and either mail it with your payment to the Albany address listed on the ticket or bring your payment to any TVB office.
You may not plead guilty by mail if the charge will result in license or registration suspension or revocation upon conviction (such as driving without insurance or a third speeding violation within 18 months). If you plead guilty to such a charge by mail, you will be notified that you must go to the TVB to answer the charge in person.

The law requires an adjustment to your monthly Medicare Part B medical insurance and Medicare prescription drug coverage premiums, but this affects less than five percent of people with Medicare, and most people don't pay higher premiums.
For most beneficiaries, the government pays a substantial portion (about 75 percent) of the Part B premium, and the beneficiary pays the remaining 25 percent.
If you have higher income, you'll pay an additional premium amount called the income-related monthly adjustment amount. For Part B, higher-income beneficiaries pay monthly premiums equal to 35, 50, 65, 80, or 85 percent of the total cost, depending on what they report to the IRS.
For Medicare prescription drug coverage, most beneficiaries have the government pay a major portion of the total costs and the beneficiary pays the rest. Higher-income beneficiaries pay monthly premiums plus an additional amount based on what they report to the IRS.
If you file taxes as married filing jointly and your MAGI is greater than $170,000, or if you file using a different status and your MAGI is greater than $85,000, you'll pay higher premiums for Part B and Medicare prescription drug coverage.
If you have limited resources and income, you may be able to get Extra Help with the costs of monthly premiums, annual deductibles, and prescription copayments related to Medicare prescription drug coverage.

Yes. If you have extenuating circumstances relating to the adverse credit history, you may still become eligible for a Direct PLUS Loan by completing PLUS Credit Counseling and providing a statement explaining your extenuating circumstances along with applicable supporting documentation.
The Secretary may use discretion and, based on your circumstances, consider whether extenuating circumstances allow you to qualify for a loan. Review does not guarantee approval, and previous approval does not guarantee further approvals.
Examples of extenuating circumstances include: being an authorized user on the account, the account being paid in full, a satisfactory repayment arrangement with six months of voluntary, consecutive, on-time, full monthly payments, the debt being included in a Chapter 13 bankruptcy, debt consolidation, or divorce (for 90+ days delinquent debts). Loss of a job or a poor economy alone are generally not considered extenuating circumstances.
Additional documentation may be required beyond the basic requirements listed, and specific proof is required for each type of extenuating circumstance (for example, a final divorce decree, a letter from the debt consolidation company, or documentation on creditor letterhead).

If you filed a federal income tax return in the past two years and your current income isn't significantly different from the income on your most recent return, your AGI will be used. You can provide your AGI by applying online using the IRS Data Retrieval Tool, or by submitting a paper Income-Driven Repayment Plan Request with a copy of your most recently filed federal tax return or IRS tax return transcript.
If your current income is significantly different from your most recent federal tax return (for example, you lost your job or experienced a drop in income), alternative documentation of your income will be used instead. You can provide this by submitting a paper request with documentation such as a pay stub, or by indicating on the application that you currently have no income or only untaxed income.

For a child under age 18, we don't need to consider the child's disability when deciding if he or she qualifies for benefits as your dependent. The child's benefits normally stop at age 18 unless he or she is a full-time student in elementary or high school (benefits can continue until age 19) or is disabled.
To apply for a child under age 18, you will need to complete an Application for Supplemental Security Income (SSI) and a Child Disability Report. At this time, only the Child Disability Report can be completed online; contact Social Security by phone or in person to schedule an appointment to complete the SSI application.
You should review the Child Disability Starter Kit, which answers common questions about applying for SSI benefits for children and includes a worksheet to help gather needed information. You should also contact Social Security right away to find out whether the income and resources of the parents and the child are within the allowed limits.
You can call toll-free at 1-800-772-1213, or the TTY number 1-800-325-0778 if you are deaf or hard of hearing. Representatives are available Monday through Friday between 8 a.m. and 5:30 p.m.

Yes, you can keep your CDL with restrictions. If you self-certify to an excepted driving type (EA or EI), a Medical Examiner's Certificate is not required, but you will need to have the appropriate restrictions added to your license (A3 and/or K).
For example, if you do not meet the USDOT federal medical requirements and cannot obtain a Medical Examiner's Certificate, but were able to keep your CDL because it was issued prior to 9/9/1999, you are eligible for Excepted Intrastate operation (EA). You must ensure your CDL has the required restrictions: K (CDL Intrastate Only) and A3 (Med Cert Exempt).
If your driving type changes, you must go into a local DMV office to change your self-certification driving type and have your license amended to add or delete the appropriate restrictions. A transaction fee will apply.
